claims.text: The initial material is an equiatomic HfNbTaTiZr random solid solution with a BCC structure.
Atomic-size mismatch causes significant lattice distortion in random HfNbTaTiZr.
Thermal annealing or controlled cooling can induce HfTi- and TiZr-type chemical short-range order in HfNbTaTiZr.
The induced short-range order forms percolating networks of ordered B2-like binary clusters.
SRO clusters can form without macroscopic phase separation below the order-disorder transition and above the glass transition.
A percolation threshold of SRO clusters must be reached for the proposed conductivity increase.
A percolating B2-like network locally regularizes the lattice potential.
Local ordering reduces force-constant fluctuations and atomic displacement amplitudes relative to the random HfNbTaTiZr state.
Random FeCoCrMnNi exhibits approximately 20% force-constant fluctuations.
Phonon broadening in random FeCoCrMnNi is primarily associated with force-constant disorder.
Ordered clusters lower the high-frequency phonon scattering rate in HfNbTaTiZr.
Percolating ordered clusters create phonon-transport pathways with an extended mean free path.
Ordering shifts the high-frequency phonon DOS from a broadened, glass-like distribution toward a sharper, Debye-like distribution.
Percolated SRO produces a net increase in HfNbTaTiZr lattice thermal conductivity relative to the random alloy.
The conductivity increase is accompanied by reduced high-frequency phonon linewidths.
Ordering shifts the Ioffe-Regel limit to higher energies.
Random HfNbTaTiZr has low thermal conductivity because of scattering from force-constant and mass fluctuations.
Below the SRO percolation threshold, HfNbTaTiZr retains random-alloy-like low conductivity.
Growth of the B2-like clusters into large precipitates reverses the effect and reduces conductivity through strong scattering.
FeCoCrMnNi exhibits a transition between scattering regimes characterized by frequency exponents of approximately 4.5 and 1.7.
